topic: How can satellite orbital altitude and inclination be optimized to minimize atmospheric turbulence impact on continuous variable quantum key distribution link budgets?
consensus_response: To optimize satellite orbital altitude and inclination for minimizing atmospheric turbulence impact on CV-QKD link budgets, consider the trade-off between uplink and downlink losses due to diffraction and beam wandering effects. Placing critical quantum technology on board exploits better downlink conditions where diffraction-induced photon losses are less significant. This approach can lead to higher entanglement distribution rates and QKD performance by reducing photon losses in the downlink channel, enabling more efficient use of available capacity.
reference_context: Satellite-based CV-QKD systems suffer from high uplink losses (25-30 dB) due to atmospheric turbulence, while downlink channels have lower losses (5-10 dB). Recent experimental deployments have exploited favorable downlink conditions, and placing critical quantum technology on board can improve performance.
